hook: You do not need millions of followers to make a living online.

blocks.narration: You do not need millions of followers to make a living online. A famous essay argues you need about one thousand true fans.
blocks.visual: Bold poster-style graphic of a small glowing crowd of one thousand dots forming a heart, orange and navy

blocks.narration: In two thousand eight, Kevin Kelly, a co-founder of Wired magazine, wrote an essay called one thousand true fans.
blocks.visual: A vintage magazine page flutters open on a desk under a warm lamp

blocks.narration: A true fan is someone who buys almost everything you make. They will drive to see you and preorder the next thing.
blocks.visual: A single dot in the crowd lights up brightly and follows a creator figure everywhere

blocks.narration: Here is the math. If one thousand true fans each spend one hundred dollars a year with you, that is one hundred thousand dollars.
blocks.visual: The heart of dots pulses as coin streams flow from each dot into one jar

blocks.narration: Not millions of casual viewers. Just one thousand people who genuinely care about what you create, year after year.
blocks.visual: A huge faint crowd fades into the background while the bright thousand stays sharp

blocks.narration: That changes the whole strategy. Instead of chasing viral reach, you focus on serving a smaller group deeply and directly.
blocks.visual: The creator figure turns from a giant megaphone to sit down and talk with the small crowd

blocks.narration: Newsletters, memberships, digital products, and courses all work this way. You own the relationship with your audience, instead of an algorithm.
blocks.visual: Small icons orbit the crowd: an envelope, a key card, a book, and a play button

blocks.narration: Reach gets you attention, but depth is what pays the bills. Follow if you are building something of your own.
blocks.visual: The glowing heart of dots grows warmer as the camera pulls back

cta: Follow if you are building something of your own.

captions.hook_line: You don't need millions of followers. You need 1,000 true fans 🎯
captions.body: In 2008, Wired co-founder Kevin Kelly argued that a creator with 1,000 true fans each spending $100 a year earns $100,000. The idea: depth of support beats raw reach for a small, independent business.

youtube_title: Why You Only Need 1,000 True Fans
